steps.text: Fill a large pot with lightly salted water and bring to a rolling boil over high heat. Stir in the egg noodles; return to a boil. Cook, uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the noodles are cooked through, but still firm to the bite, about 5 minutes. Drain; return to the pot and stir in the butter.
Meanwhile, place the bacon in a large, deep skillet, and cook over medium-high heat, turning occasionally, until evenly browned, about 10 minutes. Drain the bacon slices on a paper towel-lined plate.

Place the onion into the skillet with the bacon grease, and cook and stir over medium heat until the onion begins to soften, about 2 minutes. Stir in the cabbage, and cook and stir until wilted, about 5 minutes. Chop the bacon, add it to the skillet, and cook until the cabbage is tender, about 10 minutes. Stir in the noodles, and continue cooking just until heated through.

review.reviewBody: Hi, just so you know this is not an Irish recipe, this is however Hungarian. And, this is a good recipe.

This was very good. I cooked it pretty much as is, but since I had a large head of cabbage I used a 12 oz package of noodles and a whole pound of bacon. I did drain off some bacon grease but still used quite a bit, it is important to the flavor of the dish. I also added some salt when I first put the cabbage in the pan to help pull out the water and a sprinkle of sugar towards the end to cut any bitterness. My husband was very upset that I was adding in his noodles and his beloved bacon to the evil vegetable, but then he said it was good and had thirds!! My teenager who doesn't like ham had it as her entire meal, it is filling enough to stand on it's own. I have a ton of leftovers and can't wait to eat it again!

The roots of this dish is Lack of Money (make noodles from the pantry) and last fall's cabbage still available in the cold cellar. This recipe is perfect as is. Want to change it up? USE sliced, shredded, or bite-size pieces -- OTHER members of the cabbage family: Brussels sprouts, kohlrabi, broccoli, cauli, AND/OR kale. Also, optionally add leftover protein or scramble some eggs.

My wife and I have cut meat out of our diet, so instead of 1/2 lb. of bacon, I cooked up 2 slices of diced Tempeh based vegetarian bacon and fried that in olive oil. In place of the egg noodles I boiled up and rinsed some quinoa and brown rice based ziti noodles, and drizzled Olive oil over them once they were added to the cooked cabbage. Salt and pepper to taste, came out really good.

SO good! Being Polish, we sometimes call dishes like this, 'Lazy Pierogi'. (It's cabbage here, but in another recipe, it could be cottage or farmer's cheese added.) I don't normally use bacon when cooking cabbage, but I had some bacon grease in the fridge, so I started with that and a little olive oil for the onion. The cabbage was done in 15 min, as stated, and I added a little butter as it cooked. I also added a little black pepper and garlic powder. I pan-fried slices of kielbasa, and that went great with this. Just a little spicy brown mustard on the side to complete this. Dzienkuje (thanks) for this very good recipe!

I made this last night. I really liked it. I thought it was a little bland, so I added about 1/2 cap of apple cider vinegar and some soy sauce. And that did the trick. Also, I didn't have any egg noodles and only had wheat macaroni. So, I used those. 
Overall, I love this and I will definitely make again.

I love this kind of comfort food! I did add a little minced garlic, salt and black pepper to enhance the wonderful taste of the cabbage. I cooked as directed then sent it into the oven for awhile covered to let all the flavors come together while i did some other chores. Turned out amazing!

I drained most of the grease, only reserving about 3 Tbl, using 1 to fry the onion and the rest for the cabbage. I added 1 Tbl caraway seeds, some ground white pepper and used 12 oz noodles (just to increase the number of servings because we have a big family). It was really yummy and we really enjoyed it! Thank you for the recipe!

For someone who does not care for cabbage, this recipe was amazing.
I hate cooking bacon so I just threw in real bacon bits. This recipe by itself was delicious. I also tried adding a crushed up package of oriental Ramen Noodles and half the package of seasoning right before it was served. It was amazing! My brother in law had three helpings. It gave it a little crunch and a little more flavor. This will defiantly be my go to cabbage recipe.
I added a half quart of homemade saurcrout 1/4 cup milk 1/3 Tble spoon spiced garlic salt and 3/4 cup of bacon bits (Cosco) This was very bland before.

Well I almost never ate cabbage just like that. Why not my tongue asked my brain (busy with tastefull discrimination) ...
I followed the Idea and all the parts. Simple and don't overdo it ... I thought about the timing too (but once together the basic elements like cabbage, butter, onion, heat, spices, noodles and paprika just find their own way. It is signed after the top of old smoky paprika and Time (x3). I added a pulled Country Rib (pork) to chase the other bits around and make it whole and it Was! It was delicious. I wondered if I'd like it and it was like the reviews that helped me out in transit ... It really surprised and could appeal to many (for 2 more add a third pinch of sugar ). Very good certainly to be a repeater and if I live long enough a Classic.

All my life I’ve ever only eaten cabbage in coleslaw…. And hated it. It was right up there with jelly salads in my taste repertoire. Until I came across this recipe, or one just like it a few years ago. Now it’s my favorite comfort food. It’s still good if you have no noodles, or if you have no bacon! One reviewer mentioned hers was a little dry. Sometimes I give it a splash of vegetable broth with the cabbage. But this is a feel good staple in my kitchen. Thank you!
Grew up With this, and I love it!

I didn't like this recipe at all. I adjusted the noodles down to 6 ounces and it still was overwhelmingly more noodles than anything else. I also decreased the amount of butter since between that and the bacon fat it was pretty heavy on the fat content. Even with additional seasoning it was pretty bland for our taste.
I doubled the recipe so I could have leftovers for lunch. Tasted even better the next day.
Easy to make. Tastes great. I added extra bacon because you can never have to much. Family loved it
Absolutely delicious! Tastes like pork egg rolls only easy to make.
Really loved this cabbage recipe.
I love this recipe! Sometimes I use napa cabbage instead of regular.
A little dry. Added some white wine.
